title: Modular monolith — written update
situation: In a technical discussion, an interviewer asks why the project has one deployable unit. You must write the decision accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Write four sentences on the boundaries inside the single unit, what they buy, and when splitting would become justified.

vocabulary.meaning: the reasoning that ties a structural choice to a constraint, rather than to a trend
a separation enforced inside one deployable unit, which keeps the option of splitting later without paying for it now

expectedElements: The single unit is defended by a constraint, not by taste
A condition that would justify splitting is named
modelAnswer: The project ships as one deployable unit because every additional deployable is operational cost carried by a small team with no platform engineers. Inside the unit the modules are separated: each owns its data and is reached through an explicit interface rather than a shared table, so the option of splitting later remains open without being paid for now. Splitting would be justified by evidence that one module needs to scale or release independently of the others. Neither condition holds today.
commonMistakes: Defending the single unit as simpler without naming the constraint behind it
Claiming modularity without describing what enforces the boundaries
variants: Rewrite the update as the architecture section of a project brief.
